chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: Treatment in Miami Beach
summary: They were well treated, invited to see Walter Winchell, because Cubans were not considered black.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I see, and how were you treated?
Okay, now did you have any problems over any of those clubs?
Was there ever a time on the beach or any place where they didn't want the Machito band to appear?
No, as a matter of fact, Walter Winchell one day, one night, he has a night for him and Noro Morales was
Yeah, the Beachcomber, and we was there about ten or eleven out of my band, and we were received and we enjoyed tremendously.
I see, so then you didn't have no problem at all down in Miami Beach.
There was no problem because we were from Cuba and they consider the Cubans they are not black.
